To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the size-fractionation of the particulate trace metal inventory in the North Atlantic Ocean is controlled by lithogenic particle inputs from a variety of sources, and by biologically driven aggregation and disaggregation processes; 2) lithogenic particle cycling is a key process in determining the size-fractionated particulate trace metal distributions; 3) the lithogenic model developed in this work provides a framework for understanding the dynamics of particle cycling in the North Atlantic; 4) this framework

(i) lithogenic particle distributions in the North Atlantic are dominated by inputs from African dust and North American boundary interactions; (ii) these inputs are strongly modulated by biologically driven aggregation and disaggregation processes, which are in turn modulated by the biological pump; and (iii) the lithogenic particle distributions are strongly size-fractionated, with the largest fraction of the lithogenic material residing in the >51 µM size-fraction
the lithogenic particle distributions are strongly controlled by a variety of inputs and processes, and that the lithogenic tracer Ti is a useful tool for studying these processes.
